ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Approximately 70% high-intensity white pixels to 30% low-intensity black/dark-grey pixels across the visible ventral area.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: A central, low-intensity 'bowtie' region radiates from the peduncle into the medial lobes. Broad, high-intensity white contiguous fields occupy the majority of the lateral lobes. A thin, low-intensity border follows the trailing edge. Distinct small, dark circular pigmentation blobs are located in the upper-middle region of the left lobe.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep, symmetrical V-shaped depression with a pixel-angle of approximately 52 degrees and a depth of roughly 12% relative to the maximum fluke height.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Continuous high-frequency serration along the trailing edge with variations ranging from 2 to 10 pixels in amplitude. Serration density is highest on the outer lateral thirds of both lobes.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Trailing edges follow a convex trajectory from the notch to the lateral tips; lateral tips show a sharp, slightly downward-curving taper.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: High-density clusters of circular white pixel rings (barnacle colonies) are concentrated on the far lateral tips of both lobes. Smaller, lower-intensity white circular scars are scattered across the interior of the left lobe.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: A prominent vertical dark linear mark is visible on the mid-left lobe; several faint, unaligned horizontal scratches are detected on the lower left lobe surface.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Extensive barnacle colonization on both lateral tips resulting in irregular physical boundaries; multiple circular surface lesions on the left lobe pigmentation.
other_distinctive_markers: A highly unique dark 'spectacle' or 'figure-8' shaped pigmentation mark is located in the upper-medial region of the left fluke lobe.
